s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with localized tenderness and signs of peritoneal irritation
salient_findings: Localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium
Positive McBurney’s sign and rebound tenderness
key_facts: No history of abdominal surgery, trauma, or chronic illness

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with localized tenderness and signs of peritoneal irritation
salient_findings: Localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium
Positive McBurney’s sign and rebound tenderness
key_facts: No history of abdominal surgery, trauma, or chronic illness

shortlist.label: Midgut volvulus
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal superior mesenteric artery-vein relationship and clustered small-bowel loops on CT scan

shortlist.label: Internal hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal location of small-bowel loops and mesenteric congestion on CT scan

shortlist.label: Malrotation of the intestine
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure on CT scan

shortlist.label: Intussusception
shortlist.why_kept: Acute abdominal pain and signs of peritoneal irritation

shortlist.label: Small bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Clustered small-bowel loops and mesenteric congestion on CT scan

raw.rationale: The abnormal position of the small-bowel loops, the abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, and the abnormal superior mesenteric artery-vein relationship on the CT scan are consistent with malrotation of the intestine.

rejected.label: Midgut volvulus
rejected.why: While possible, the lack of signs of ischemia and the specific CT findings make malrotation a more direct explanation.

rejected.label: Internal hernia
rejected.why: The CT findings do not specifically indicate an internal hernia, and other signs such as bowel obstruction are not prominent.

rejected.label: Intussusception
rejected.why: The CT scan did not show the characteristic target sign of intussusception, and the clinical presentation does not strongly suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Small bowel obstruction
rejected.why: While the patient has abdominal pain, the normal bowel sounds and lack of distention, along with the specific CT findings, make malrotation a more specific diagnosis than a general obstruction.
